This packet also includes a vote to compensate land owners for each individual taking. We are requesting that the City Council hold a public hearing and consider voting on this matter at their September 16, 2026 meeting. The City was awarded an FY2025 HousingWorks grant to address public safety and accessibility concerns at the Parsons Street and Ferry Street intersection. This grant funds work to improve vehicle sightlines and to increase pedestrian safety and connectivity by creating a new sidewalk on the south side of Ferry Street. In order to accomplish these improvements, an existing retaining wall will be relocated several feet back from the roadway. Additionally, two crosswalks with rapid-flashing beacons will be installed on Ferry Street. These improvements require the City to acquire permanent and temporary construction easements on a total of eight properties. The City has communicated with all affected property owners since April 2026 and recently acquired appraisals for the permanent and temporary easements. Owners of two properties donated their easements to the City and Just Compensation Reports for the remaining properties were sent to owners in July 2026, along with notification of the City Council public hearing. The project design plans and easement plans are posted on the Planning Department website (https://www.easthamptonma.gov/978/Ferry-Street-HousingWorks-Infrastructure). The City’s team includes the City Planner, City Engineer and DPW Director, the design consultant (VHB), the City’s appraiser (Crowley and Associates), and the City Solicitor. The requested action from City Council includes voting on the Order of Taking to take the easements and an appropriation of $50,810 to pay property owners from the Parsons & Ferry Intersection Capital Project account. The following information is included in this packet: 1. Resolution 2. Order of Taking a. Exhibit A - Order of Taking with Exhibits b. Exhibit B - Chart of Payments c. Exhibit C - Donations 3.
